A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Antidistillation Sampling. Their text, equations, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including the example traces that require visual inspection.

before.justification: v1 reports original GSM8K and MATH distillation results, a permutation-sampling comparison, and numerical finite-difference validation.

after.justification: v3 reports original distillation experiments, including MMLU evaluations, additional model configurations, loss trajectories and JVP comparisons.

M1.justification: v1 Equation 11 uses forward finite differences; v3 Equations 10 and 13 prescribe centered differences using positively and negatively perturbed proxy weights. This locally changes penalty computation while retaining the poisoning objective. However, v3 Algorithm 1 and Figure 2 retain the forward-difference description, leaving the implemented variant unclear.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluated MMLU coverage to v1's GSM8K and MATH experiments, substantially extending evaluation beyond mathematical reasoning to broader multitask knowledge and reasoning. The original mathematical tasks remain.

E2.justification: Temperature sampling and permutation sampling remain evaluated comparators. v3 Figure 8 additionally compares downstream student accuracy against JVP-based sampling; v1 used JVP only as a numerical reference for derivative-approximation error.

E3.justification: The reported finite-difference step changes from 10^-4 to 10^-2, and approximation validation changes from GPT2-Large to Qwen2.5-3B. v3 also adds all-Qwen/all-Llama configurations and a Float32 finite-difference-versus-JVP evaluation. The stated LoRA settings and four-epoch distillation budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds training-versus-holdout loss analysis (Figure 5), downstream finite-difference/JVP validation (Figure 8), and same-family architecture checks (Figure 10). It revises numerical approximation validation to use the actual proxy model. The permutation ablation and three example-trace studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions display shaded uncertainty bands, but v3 Appendix B.2 first identifies means and 95% confidence intervals from bootstrapped LOWESS fits. Neither version specifies independent training-run counts or seeds, so an increase in experimental repetitions is not established.

E6.justification: v3 replaces the main GSM8K and approximation-error curves and adds MMLU/MATH trade-off curves, architecture/JVP results and loss trajectories. Figure 5 newly shows training loss decreasing while holdout loss increases. The permutation plot and example traces are retained. Revised settings prevent treating changed scores as demonstrated same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The finite-epsilon penalty definition changes from a forward-difference estimator to a centered-difference estimator. The underlying loss-change objective, gradient-inner-product identity, limiting derivative and assumptions remain unchanged; Appendix C largely restates the existing mathematical rationale.

C1.justification: Both abstracts and conclusions retain the central proof-of-concept claim that modifying next-token probabilities can poison distillation while preserving teacher utility. The expanded benchmark examples provide further support for this retained contribution.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the loss trajectories as showing traces that remain learnable but damage generalization (Section 4.4). It also adds a security argument contrasting hidden-proxy perturbations with static defenses, discusses high-teacher-accuracy operating points, and quantifies approximately doubled sampling computation. These substantially expand v1's brief interpretation.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents the 70/30 training/holdout split, teacher-generated holdout traces, gradient accumulation and prompt masking, answer extraction, generation limits, GSM8K Platinum testing, and hardware/software. It also supplies an explicit code-repository link. These disclosures do not establish that every corresponding experimental setting changed.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands related work on compression and context distillation and adds a distillation-prevention discussion covering Undistillable, Stingy Teacher, watermarking and QUEEN. It newly positions its token-wise perturbations against static and session-dynamic defenses, beyond v1's general poisoning and controlled-decoding positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Related work becomes a standalone section, the method overview becomes a subsection, experiments are reorganized around setup, trade-offs, configurations and generalization, and the appendices are reordered.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the opening bar-chart display with a workflow schematic, adds a proxy-gradient diagram and several result panels, and redraws the main trade-off plot. Figure 9 magnifies existing sweeps. The permutation plot and example-trace panels are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v1's limited validation and missing reproduction details through MMLU evaluation, architecture and JVP checks, loss-dynamics evidence, and approximation validation on the actual proxy model. It also explains gradient construction and uncertainty bands. These gains outweigh the localized inconsistency between the centered-difference equations and unchanged forward-difference pseudocode and illustration, although that inconsistency still limits reproducibility.
